text:
mike: quick heads-up — hit a rare assert in the allocator drain after the inflight prefetch patch landed. dumping findings here so we don't lose it

tara: ugh, which assert? stack?

mike: assertion: "drain: no outstanding reservations allowed" in alloc.cc:421
stack:
```
#0  0x7f8c1a2b in drain()
#1  0x7f8c1a7e in prefetch_completion_cb()
#2  0x7f8c1b00 in worker_thread()
```
repro: stress run against staging, `./tools/prefetch_stress --clients=200 --seq=8192`

jia: did we get a reproducer outside stress env? ci or a unit test?

mike: only on staging with high RPS so far. I added a small harness that flips prefetch on/off in tight loop, seems flaky. sending link: https://staging/logs/4871-prefetch-err (internal)

sam: @mike can you paste the flow diagram of prefetch vs reservation? i'm fuzzy on exact ownership semantics when prefetch completes and drain is racing

mike: brief: request -> reserve pages (alloc API) -> issue prefetch -> prefetch can complete after allocator drain requested (drain waits for all inflight reservations to be released). bug seems to be prefetch completion callback still holding a transient ref when drain thinks none exist.

tara: could be missing refcount bump on the callback handoff? or callback running on a worker that didn't pin reservation?

mike: i instrumented refcounts — they go 1 -> 0 inside callback but drain checks for >0 earlier and fails. ordering windows are small but show up under contention.

jia: idea: introduce a short-lived "callback-hold" which increments reservation ref on callback entry and decrements on exit. then drain should treat that as inflight. but that means drain has to consider both reservation refs and callback-hold refs.

sam: we already have reservation refs and a separate inflight counter for IO. maybe unify them? pros/cons?

tara: unify would be cleaner but larger change surface. quick win: make drain check the inflight IO counter in addition to refs. but we need to guarantee callback increments inflight counter before drain snapshot. race still possible if drain does a snapshot before increment.

mike: right — snapshot races. alternative: make drain a two-phase: 1) set draining flag, 2) wait for the *quiescent* state where no new callbacks can start (callbacks check draining flag and either increment or fail fast). callbacks that see draining flag must still complete but they first increment a special counter under a lock that drain then waits on.

sam: that's basically handshaking. More overhead but localized. What's the perf impact?

mike: microbench shows ~0.2% p50 latency increase in worst case (when draining frequently). in normal steady-state no drain, overhead is nil.

jia: long-term we should enforce an invariant: any path that may touch allocator state must acquire a lightweight lease (rc or seq). could be the foundation for other fixes (compaction, eviction).

tara: agree — but for immediate safety i'd prefer the handshaking + short counter approach. patch should include telemetry: counter for drain-waits, average wait time, and how often callbacks see draining flag.

mike: i'll draft a PR with the handshaking change + tests. plan:
- add draining flag + callback pre-check
- callback increments callback-hold counter under atomic if allowed
- drain sets flag then waits on counter==0
- add unit test that forces callback race and checks no assert
- add telemetry counters

sam: please also include a kill-switch config so we can flip to old behavior if needed in canary.

mike: will do. @infra-bot can you schedule a canary rollout for my branch after CI passes?

infra-bot: scheduled canary for branch mike/prefetch-drain-fix on cluster:staging-canary at 2026-04-02T09:00Z :white_check_mark:

jia: thanks — once PR is up i'll try to add a compactness integration test to exercise compaction+prefetch+drain combos.

tara: maybe also add a debug trace that logs when drain starts and finishes along with current inflight counters (sampled). that helped me before.

mike: good call. i'll add tracepoints and a shortdoc in the PR. aiming to open today.

sam: awesome. tag me and i'll review.

mike: thanks everyone, will post PR link here.
